findings.title: Demo hardcodes distances derived from behavior tuning constants

If behavior.ts tuning changes, the demo silently stops surfacing the ANGRY/SINGING tiers it exists to showcase; deriving offsets from the now-exported constants would keep it in sync.

findings.title: ANGRY trigger is shadowed by the flee check for continuous movement
findings.desc: EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE (0.6) sits inside the committed EATING flee threshold (base×0.4, ≈1.6 at base 4.0, and still ≈0.8 at full stealth), so any continuous approach crosses the flee threshold first and the creature FLEEs before the player can ever be within 0.6 while it's still EATING — for typical phenotypes ANGRY is only reachable by teleporting, which is exactly what the demo and both sim tests do, masking the gap. Only bottom-range fleeDistance phenotypes at max stealth (base×0.2 < 0.6) make the tier reachable through actual play, contradicting the "deliberate-to-trigger close approach" intent.

findings.title: Interrupted SINGING grants CONTENT, which immediately cancels the FLEE it caused
findings.desc: onEnterState arms the CONTENT mood (flee multiplier 0.5) when SINGING exits via FLEE, so next tick the interrupting player (e.g. at 3–5 units) is outside the halved threshold and the creature returns to WANDER after ~1 tick, becoming *more* approachable to the player who just ruined the song. The doc justifies granting the mood ("deliberate small mercy") but doesn't acknowledge that it collapses the documented "interrupting a song is the failure mode players learn to avoid" punishment.

findings.title: Module header still claims the flee event "interrupts anything"

findings.title: Interrupted songs retain an active timer
findings.desc: `onEnterState` sets `singingTimer` when entering `SINGING` but never clears it when transitioning to `FLEE`. A song interrupted while its timer is still positive therefore leaves a nonzero singing timer on a non-singing creature, contradicting the timer’s state semantics and potentially misleading renderers or other consumers.

findings.title: Interrupted songs retain an active singing timer
findings.desc: When SINGING transitions to FLEE, `onEnterState` sets CONTENT mood but never clears `singingTimer`, leaving a positive timer while the creature is no longer singing. findings.title: Expired SINGING can still transition to FLEE
findings.desc: The SINGING branch checks the raised flee distance before checking whether `singingTimer` has expired. On the tick the timer reaches zero, a player within the singer’s threshold can produce `FLEE` instead of ending the song and returning to `WANDER`, contrary to the documented timer lifecycle and the generic post-song behavior.

findings.title: Interrupted songs incorrectly grant CONTENT mood
findings.desc: `onEnterState` sets CONTENT whenever the creature leaves SINGING, including when the song is interrupted by FLEE. This also applies the CONTENT multiplier while the creature is still in FLEE, potentially shrinking its flee distance and causing it to abandon fleeing immediately even while the player remains nearby; the documented mood is described as a post-SINGING return state.

findings.title: Missing else clause in ANGRY trigger could cause fallthrough
findings.desc: The ANGRY trigger block lacks an else or early return, so after checking for EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE, the function proceeds to the flee check; this could cause an ANGRY creature to incorrectly flee if the player is also within the effective flee distance (though ANGRY should ignore flee check). However, line 206 returns "ANGRY", so the function exits; this is correct, but the formatting may mislead.

findings.title: Potential mood timer reset on state re-entry
findings.desc: In onEnterState, when transitioning from ANGRY or SINGING to another state, the mood and moodTimer are set, but if the creature re-enters the same state (e.g., ANGRY again), the mood may be overwritten incorrectly; this is a minor edge case, but could affect mood persistence.

findings.title: Test may be inaccurate due to stealth factor
findings.desc: The test for an EATING creature tolerating a stealthy approach uses distance 0.9, playerStealth 1, and claims it is outside the threshold (0.8). However, stealth reduces the threshold; with full stealth, threshold = 4.0 * 0.4 * 0.5 = 0.8. Since 0.9 > 0.8, the creature should keep EATING, which matches the expectation, so the test is correct, but the comment incorrectly states 0.7 < 0.8 would flee.

findings.title: Demo comment mismatch with behavior
findings.desc: The demo comment says "SINGING/ANGRY expressive tiers" but the demo only provokes ANGRY in phase 2 and SINGING in phase 1; it does not capture both in the same moment, which is fine, but the phrasing could be clearer.

findings.title: Incorrect test logic in flee interrupt test
findings.desc: The test says "player is inside the committed threshold but OUTSIDE the interrupt distance" but uses distance 1.0 which is INSIDE the committed threshold (1.6) but OUTSIDE interrupt (0.6). However, the comment incorrectly states the player is "inside that (so the creature spooks)" – actually 1.0 < 1.6 means inside threshold, so spook occurs. The test logic is correct but the comment is misleading about spooking.

findings.title: Post-ANGRY WANDER test might not reflect real behavior
findings.desc: The test checks that ANGRY with timer 0 returns to WANDER, but in real execution, leaving ANGRY sets mood to WARY via onEnterState. The test passes because mood is not used in that specific expectation, but the creature would actually be in WANDER with WARY mood, not NEUTRAL as implied by default ctx.

findings.title: ANGRY trigger condition may incorrectly override FLEE
findings.desc: The ANGRY trigger checks if distance <= EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE *while* the state is EATING. However, if player is inside interrupt distance AND also inside effectiveFleeDistance, ANGRY should trigger (as coded). But if player is inside interrupt but outside effectiveFleeDistance (e.g., high stealth), creature should stay EATING, not get ANGRY. The code seems correct because flee check is after ANGRY trigger, but ordering ensures ANGRY wins if inside interrupt regardless of flee distance – which matches design (invasion provokes anger even if stealthy).

findings.title: Redundant effectiveFleeDistance call in SINGING check
findings.desc: In SINGING block, effectiveFleeDistance(ctx) is called for flee check, but later in generic flee check (line 267) it's called again if state not ANGRY/SINGING. This could be optimized by storing result, but not critical.

findings.title: onEnterState sets mood on exit incorrectly for interrupted states
findings.desc: The function sets mood on exit from ANGRY or SINGING regardless of what state is entered. If ANGRY -> FLEE (e.g., player runs away during anger), mood would still be set to WARY, which may be unintended. Design likely wants mood only when returning to WANDER, but spec says "leaving SINGING -> CONTENT" total. This could cause CONTENT mood during FLEE which seems odd.

findings.title: Missing mood reset when entering expressive states
findings.desc: When entering ANGRY or SINGING, previous mood (e.g., CONTENT from prior song) is not cleared. This could lead to mood stacking (e.g., CONTENT mood during ANGRY). Should reset mood to NEUTRAL (or at least not apply) when entering these states, as they have their own timer-based behavior.

findings.title: Missing reset of mood when leaving ANGRY/SINGING
findings.desc: The function `onEnterState` sets mood to WARY/CONTENT when *leaving* those states, but does not reset mood to NEUTRAL when leaving other states (e.g., a mood may persist unintentionally across unrelated state transitions).

findings.title: Potential floating-point error in mood timer check
findings.desc: The check `ctx.moodTimer > 0` may be unreliable due to floating-point precision after decrementing in `stepCreature`. Use a small epsilon or ensure timers never become negative (they are clamped to max(0, ...), so `=== 0` is safe but `> 0` may still be true for very small positive values).

findings.title: ANGRY trigger may override legitimate FLEE condition
findings.desc: The ANGRY trigger (distance <= EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE) is checked before the flee check, which is correct for the design, but if the player is within both the interrupt distance and the flee distance, ANGRY wins. This is intended, but the comment should clarify that ANGRY supersedes FLEE in that overlap zone.

findings.title: Mood reset on timer zero may conflict with onEnterState
findings.desc: In `stepCreature`, `if (c.moodTimer === 0) c.mood = "NEUTRAL";` resets mood when timer expires, but `onEnterState` may later set mood again on state exit. This could cause a race if timer expires in same tick as a state transition (order dependent). The behavior is likely fine but not documented.

findings.title: Demo script comment inaccuracies
findings.desc: Comments refer to "phase 1/polite distance" and "phase 2/aggressive crowding," but the code uses `provokingPhaseStart = Math.floor(obsTicks / 2)`. The comment does not match the actual division point (halfway). Also, the camera target logic may not align with described behavior.

findings.desc: `EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE` (0.6) is a constant while the EATING committed flee threshold is `phenotype.fleeDistance * 0.4` (and further shrunk by stealth). For phenotypes whose `fleeDistance` gene is small enough that `0.4 * fleeDistance` (or the stealth-reduced value) drops below 0.6, the ANGRY interrupt check fires even at distances outside the creature's own committed flee zone, and the FLEE branch for EATING becomes effectively unreachable — inverting the intended "interrupt is closer/rarer than flee" tier ordering documented in the comments.

findings.title: `onEnterState` handles both enter- and exit-side effects
findings.desc: The method name and most of its doc framing describe it as firing "on entering ANGRY/SINGING," but it also performs exit-triggered mood assignment (`from === "ANGRY"/"SINGING"`) on every transition, including transitions that don't involve ANGRY/SINGING as the destination. This dual responsibility under an "enter" name is easy to misread when this logic is extended later (e.g. someone adding a new enter-only side effect might not realize exit logic is co-located here).

findings.title: Tier ladder comment no longer names an explicit tier for FLEE
findings.desc: The header explicitly maps FSM states onto the "Common/Uncommon/Rare/Secret" tiers from initial_concept.md, but FLEE (0.75) is now described only positionally ("sits BETWEEN the uncommon eat cycle and the rare song") without being assigned one of the four named tiers, leaving the tier-to-state mapping promised by the comment incomplete/ambiguous.

findings.title: Fixed EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE can make FLEE-from-EATING unreachable
findings.desc: `EATING_INTERRUPT_DISTANCE` is a fixed 0.6 world units, not scaled by phenotype, while the committed EATING flee threshold is `base fleeDistance * 0.4`. For any phenotype whose `fleeDistance` is small enough that `fleeDistance * 0.4 <= 0.6` (or with mood/stealth further shrinking the threshold), the ANGRY check (checked before the flee check) will always fire first for any distance that would have triggered FLEE, making the "tolerant -> flee" tier unreachable and every EATING interruption resolve to ANGRY instead of the intended flee/anger split.

findings.title: Mood multiplier applies to all states, not just post-return WANDER as documented
findings.desc: The `Mood` JSDoc states the mood "modulates the flee threshold once the creature returns to WANDER," but `effectiveFleeDistance` applies `MOOD_MULTIPLIER` unconditionally for whatever `ctx.state` is (FORAGE, EATING, SINGING, etc.) as long as `moodTimer > 0`. A creature that goes WANDER(WARY) -> FORAGE/EATING within the 30s WARY window will have its FORAGE/EATING flee threshold inflated too, which the comment doesn't describe.

findings.title: Expired songs still use the SINGING flee threshold

findings.desc: The proximity check runs before checking `singingTimer`, so on the tick the timer reaches zero a player outside the normal flee range but inside the 1.4× SINGING range causes a spurious `FLEE` transition instead of ending the song into `WANDER`.

findings.title: ANGRY is unreachable through a normal gradual approach
findings.desc: An EATING creature enters FLEE as soon as the player crosses its larger effective flee threshold, so it is no longer EATING when the player later crosses the 0.6 ANGRY threshold. In typical continuous movement, ANGRY therefore requires teleporting across the outer threshold in one tick, as the tests and demo do.

findings.title: Expired songs still use the SINGING flee threshold
findings.desc: The flee check runs before checking `singingTimer > 0`, so on the expiration tick a player outside the normal WANDER threshold but inside the raised SINGING threshold incorrectly causes FLEE instead of the documented return to WANDER.

findings.title: Demo's fixed singer distance is not guaranteed safe
findings.desc: The 6.5-unit camera distance assumes a base flee distance of 4.0, but `effectiveFleeDistance` is phenotype-dependent; singers with a base distance above roughly 4.64 will be interrupted before capture, undermining the claim that the deterministic demo surfaces SINGING.
